message.content:
The 200 events below are a random draw, without replacement, from about 44,600 photon interactions recorded in the scoring volume. They come from an analog Monte Carlo I wrote in numpy, since no transport code was available. Approximations: Compton uses the free-electron Klein-Nishina formula with a flat 2% binding reduction (no scattering function); Rayleigh uses a small-angle Gaussian; photoelectric angles use a Sauter-like law; pair-electron angles are approximate; bremsstrahlung and fluorescence are not modelled. Cross sections are checked against NIST water values at 0.1–1 MeV to within about 1.5%. The pair-production cross section at 2 MeV (about 1.45e-3 cm²/g) is my estimate, not a table value.

Breakdown of the 200 sampled events: 194 Compton, 3 Rayleigh, 2 pair, 1 photoelectric. The 1.2e8-history pool gave about 96.6% Compton, 1.3% pair, 1.2% Rayleigh and 0.8% photoelectric.

Compton by Klein-Nishina rejection; annihilation photons tracked.
